content_md:
[Metascience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metascience) needs to attend to both day and night science.

[Day science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_science) is the industrialised academy: reliable, recurring increments of knowledge, delivered via shared norms and established sociotechnical systems. [Night science](https://night-science.org/) is the unlooked-for insight and [serious play](https://contraptions.venkateshrao.com/p/the-curiously-playable-universe) that throws up novel conjectures and, occasionally, paradigm shifts. Done well, they feed each other.

With AI, there’s a risk we end up in an epistemological Antarctica. *EverDay* looks like success: the pipelines churn, the metrics climb, and the anomalies that might spark something new get smoothed away as noise. *EverNight* is conjecture unmoored from evidence. It runs from [crackpot](https://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/crackpot.html) theories and ideas we can’t comprehend, to ones that sound plausible but can’t be [falsified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falsifiability).

Polar seasons, with their months-long days and nights, disorient. Like humans, science needs a circadian rhythm to function, a [tick-tock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick%E2%80%93tock_model) where ideas still answer to evidence and evidence can still surprise us. The task is to find that rhythm while respecting [Sutton’s law](https://msweet.net/notes/138-maroon-hares).
